claim.text: Is the statement described in this narrative hearsay under FRE 801(c)?

arguments.text: The narrative presents a fact ("John likes sweatpants") rather than an out-of-court statement. FRE 801(c) hearsay only applies to "statements," which require an assertion or conduct intended as an assertion. Non-assertive facts do not trigger the hearsay rule.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(a) & (c) definition of hearsay requires an out-of-court statement (assertion).
arguments.evidence_span: the fact that John likes sweatpants

arguments.text: The fact is offered to address whether John knew about the conspiracy. Because it is circumstantial evidence of state of mind or notice rather than an assertion offered for its truth, it falls outside the scope of FRE 801(c).
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) excludes evidence offered for purposes other than proving the truth of the matter asserted, such as state of mind or notice.
arguments.evidence_span: On the issue of whether John knew about the conspiracy

arguments.text: The narrative lacks any mention of a declarant or an explicit assertion being repeated. Without an assertion, the threshold requirement for hearsay under FRE 801(a) and (c) is not met.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(a) requires a 'statement,' which is an assertion or nonverbal conduct intended as an assertion.
